ai.definition: Mycelium structural composites are building materials derived from the fungal root network, or mycelium, which binds agricultural waste into lightweight, fire-resistant blocks.
ai.howItWorks: The process involves inoculating mycelium onto crop residues placed in moulds. The mycelium grows and binds the substrate together, forming a solid mass that is then dried to halt growth and set its shape.
ai.problemSolved: Reduces waste from agricultural by-products while providing an eco-friendly alternative to traditional building materials like concrete or wood.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process occurs in controlled environments such as labs or greenhouses, utilizing renewable resources and minimizing environmental impact.
ai.buildProcess: Mycelium is grown in moulds containing agricultural waste; once fully developed, the blocks are dried to halt growth and maintain their shape.
ai.costDrivers: Initial research and development costs, substrate sourcing, controlled environment requirements, and drying processes contribute to overall cost.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Expected to transition from lab research into pilot projects and commercial trials in the near future due to its promising environmental benefits and potential for scalability.
ai.regulation: Currently no specific regulations apply; however, as this technology scales, regulatory frameworks may be developed to address safety and performance standards.
ai.risks: Potential issues include inconsistent growth rates, substrate variability, and ensuring structural integrity of the final product.
ai.profitability: Uncertain at present due to limited commercial applications and high R&D costs; potential for significant cost savings in large-scale production and reduced environmental impact could drive profitability in the future.
ai.futureDevelopment: Research is expected to focus on optimizing growth conditions, improving mechanical properties, and expanding application areas beyond current research stages.

glossary.def: The vegetative part of a fungus consisting of a network of filaments called hyphae.
A material composed of two or more components, one of which is biological in nature and the other synthetic or natural but non-biological.

subsystems.name: Fungal strain and spawn
subsystems.role: provides the living binder that grows through the substrate.

subsystems.name: Lignocellulosic substrate
subsystems.role: the agricultural residue that feeds the fungus and forms the bulk of the composite.

subsystems.name: Mould and growth chamber
subsystems.role: shapes the material and keeps temperature, humidity and sterility in the right range.

subsystems.name: Mycelial network
subsystems.role: the hyphae that weave around and between particles, acting as a self-assembling adhesive.

subsystems.name: Post-processing line
subsystems.role: stops growth, removes water and can densify the material.

subsystems.name: Finishing and protection
subsystems.role: improves water resistance, fire performance and surface quality.

subsystems.name: Testing and quality control
subsystems.role: checks strength, stiffness, fire and moisture behaviour.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the substrate
buildSteps.detail: Dry and chop agricultural waste, then sterilise it to kill competing moulds and bacteria.

buildSteps.title: Inoculate
buildSteps.detail: Mix the cooled substrate with fungal spawn and water so the mycelium can colonise.

buildSteps.title: Fill the mould
buildSteps.detail: Pack the mixture into a mould of the desired shape, controlling density.

buildSteps.title: Grow the network
buildSteps.detail: Incubate in warm, humid conditions for days to weeks until white mycelium binds the particles into a solid.

buildSteps.title: Stop growth
buildSteps.detail: Heat-treat the block to kill the fungus and prevent fruiting bodies, locking in the shape.

buildSteps.title: Dry and densify
buildSteps.detail: Dry the material; if structural performance is needed, press it hot to increase density and strength.

buildSteps.title: Demould and finish
buildSteps.detail: Remove from mould, trim, sand, and apply coatings or laminate skins for water and fire resistance.

buildSteps.title: Test and certify
buildSteps.detail: Measure compressive and flexural strength, fire class and moisture uptake; iterate the recipe.

prerequisites.why: need fast-growing, non-toxic strains that bind well and do not fruit.
straw, hemp hurd and sawdust are widely available.
contamination by other microbes ruins a batch.
understanding how mycelium composites behave under load and fire is still developing.

prerequisites.tech: Standards and certification for bio-based structural materials
prerequisites.why: building codes lack approved routes for load-bearing mycelium composites.

pathway.milestone: lab-scale and prototype panels for insulation and non-structural cladding
pilot production of consistent mycelium boards and panels
pathway.unlocks: commercial use in interiors and non-load-bearing walls.

pathway.milestone: densified and hybrid mycelium composites with reinforcement
pathway.unlocks: load-bearing components such as studs, beams or floor cassettes.

pathway.milestone: certified structural systems and mainstream supply chains
